A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same KPIG research. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices support reliable comparison, including matching material moved or renumbered in v2.

before.justification: v1 reports original KPIG experiments on Sup-NatInst and Chinese Domain datasets, including baseline comparisons, ablations, and instruction-following investigations.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds InsCL comparisons, hyperparameter sensitivity results, and saliency experiments.

M1.justification: Instruction diversification, masked key-part information gain, replay selection, and the temperature-adjusted cross-entropy/JSD objective remain unchanged. Algorithm 1 is retained; the added analyses do not modify KPIG.

E1.justification: Both versions retain 128 Sup-NatInst tasks and 20 Chinese Domain tasks under single-task and single-category settings. The additional sensitivity and saliency analyses examine existing task coverage without introducing a new domain or task requirement.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds InsCL for Sup-NatInst-ST and Sup-NatInst-SC, with no corresponding Domain results. All existing benchmark comparators remain.

E3.justification: New diagnostic protocols vary replay size with M fixed, sweep lambda or alpha while fixing the other, and examine layerwise saliency on two randomly selected Sup-NatInst tasks. Existing benchmark splits, models, metrics, and selected training hyperparameters remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The diagnostic evidence expands substantially: Appendix B adds controlled lambda/alpha sensitivity results and replay-size curves comparing KPIG with DYNAINST, extending v1's qualitative replay discussion. Appendix F adds ground-truth/key-part saliency case studies. Existing component ablations and information-gain investigations remain.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random-seed specifications, confidence intervals, error bars, or formal significance tests. The added experiments retain point-estimate reporting.

E6.justification: Existing results in Tables 1–4 and Figure 4 remain unchanged. Added InsCL results change the seen-task ranking: its ST/SC P-scores are 52.5/57.1 versus KPIG's 52.2/56.5, under its larger replay allowance. Table 11 and Figures 5–6 add sensitivity and saliency outcomes, rather than improvements to previously reported KPIG scores.

T1.justification: The task definitions, information-gain equations, loss, temperature rule, and evaluation-score definitions are retained. The saliency addition is empirical and introduces no new formal derivation or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims about key-part information gain, replay and regularization, instruction-following metrics, and generalization. The added evidence does not redefine these core contributions.

C2.justification: Section 4.2 acknowledges InsCL's higher seen-task P-scores and suggests replay volume as an explanation. New appendices discuss regularization/generalization tradeoffs, limitations of fixed hyperparameters, and weaker saliency evidence for generation than classification. The original Limitations section remains unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendix C adds InsCL's maximum replay count of 200 and approximately 440-minute training time. Conversely, v1's explicit M/N search grids for both datasets disappear. Existing hardware, optimizer, model, GPT-4 version, and prompt-template details remain.

R1.justification: v2 adds InsCL (Wang et al., 2024) as a comparator and Wang et al. (2023a), Label Words Are Anchors, for saliency analysis. The related-work taxonomy and broader novelty positioning remain unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 adds Hyperparameter Sensitivity and Saliency Score appendices, separates tuning discussion from implementation, and makes localized experimental-discussion edits. Author and affiliation information changes, and acknowledgments are added; most existing prose and the main section structure remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds Figures 5–6 and the hyperparameter Table 11, and expands Table 1 with an InsCL row. Existing displays remain, with appendix reflow and the former held-out-instruction Table 11 renumbered Table 12.

improvement.justification: The InsCL comparison makes performance positioning more informative, while sensitivity results and qualified saliency findings strengthen empirical understanding of KPIG. These are useful, limited improvements to an otherwise stable paper. Removing explicit replay-search grids modestly weakens reproducibility detail, but the added comparisons and diagnostics provide a net benefit.
